(disorder)' -- verified via Ontoserver: active, International Edition core

remarks: Task 2.2 fix: this Counter previously fired exactly once (there was no path
back to it), so disease_duration_years topped out at 2 and the >=5/>=10
thresholds below were dead code -- PD-dementia unreachable, and every
survivor fell straight through to the 'else' branch (100% promoted to
MotorComplications after a single ~2-4yr StablePeriod), which is the
audit's '100% die of PD 5-8yr post-dx' finding. Fixed by looping: each
tier's non-promoted share now returns via AnnualProgressionCheck (a Delay
+ mortality reroll, ~1yr/pass) instead of forcing promotion, so duration
climbs annually and the >=10 tier -- guaranteed unreachable before -- is now
reached at ~duration 10 (roughly 8 loop passes past this state's first,
~2-4yr StablePeriod-delayed entry at duration 2), matching the fix spec's
'PD-dementia arm reachable at ~10yr duration'.
Also routes the >=10/>=5 promote branches through HoehnYahrStage3 (was:
straight to MotorComplications for the >=10/>=5 tiers, silently skipping
the h_and_y_stage=3 SetAttribute -- a pre-existing minor inconsistency,
fixed in passing since HoehnYahrStage3 already direct-transitions to
MotorComplications anyway).
Per-tier promotion hazard rises with duration (12%/yr under 5yr, 25%/yr
5-10yr, then 35% dementia / 25% motor-complications / 40% continue-looping
at 10yr+) -- a calibration approximation, not literature-exact, chosen so
cumulative promotion by year 5 lands near the ~40-50% commonly cited for
levodopa-related motor complications within 4-6 years (Ahlskog JE & Muenter
MD, 'Frequency of levodopa-related dyskinesias and motor fluctuations as
estimated from the cumulative literature', Mov Disord 2001;16(3):448-458).
The 10yr+ tier deliberately keeps a 40% continue-looping branch (not a
guaranteed 100% exit): without it, EVERY sufficiently long-lived diagnosed
patient is eventually funneled into this module's own terminal cascade with
certainty as years->infinity, which would still make PD-attributed mortality
converge to ~100% of diagnosed patients over a full-lifetime simulation --
just with realistic (rather than rigidly narrow) timing. The continue-loop
branch (each pass carrying its own 2%/yr mortality check, see
AnnualProgressionCheck) leaves room for competing causes -- Synthea's own
background all-cause mortality, or another disease module -- to end some
patients' lives first, so the eventual PD-specific-death fraction seen in a
real generation run is expected to land measurably below 100% (verified in
the Task 2.2 SMOKE run; see the module's fix-brief report for the observed
fraction). PD-dementia relative odds are essentially unchanged by this (35
vs 25 preserves the original 60/40 dementia:motor-complications ratio
conditional on eventually exiting the loop).
Task 2.2 fix: annual reroll loop (Task 1.6/alzheimers idiom) that lets
disease_duration_years keep climbing every ~year instead of the module
falling through to MotorComplications after a single pass.
Also carries two competing exits per pass, both needed to break the
otherwise-deterministic 'every sufficiently long-lived diagnosed patient
eventually reaches the motor-complications/dementia terminal cascade' funnel
(a linear once-promoted cascade -- MotorComplications->...->EndStageDisease
-- with no other branch point that isn't itself 100% death-absorbing):
- 2%/yr excess-mortality hazard. PD carries roughly 1.5-2x
general-population mortality (Macleod AD et al., 'Mortality in
Parkinson's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis', Mov Disord
2014;29(13):1615-1622); this is a modest excess-hazard approximation
layered on top of Synthea's own independent background all-cause
mortality (applied outside any disease module), not a literature-exact
per-year figure.
- 5%/yr exit to Terminal ('stable/indolent course, lost to this module's
follow-up'): not every PD patient progresses to severe motor
complications or dementia -- a meaningful minority maintain a more
indolent, often tremor-dominant course associated with slower
progression (Jankovic J, 'Parkinson's disease: clinical features and
diagnosis', J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2008;79(4):368-376). These
patients exit this module (their eventual death, from PD-unrelated
causes or old age, is Synthea's background lifecycle module's concern,
not this one's) rather than being deterministically funneled into
end-stage disease given enough simulated years. Same idiom as
alzheimers.json's Annual_MCI_Progression_Check RevertToNormal exit
(Task 1.6).
No encounter is open anywhere in this annual loop (verified by BFS), so
neither exit needs a separate close-the-visit step here.

Task 2.2 fix: dyskinesia_severe was read by MedicationAdjustment (gating

consistent with reports that a minority of levodopa-treated patients with
dyskinesia need dedicated anti-dyskinetic therapy such as amantadine).
No exact SNOMED match for 'wearing-off phenomenon in PD'. Using 427488005
'On - off phenomenon' per AAN PD Quality Measurement Set 2020 — closely related
concept covering motor fluctuations on dopaminergic therapy. Browser-confirm before
production. Wearing-off and on-off phenomena are clinically distinct (wearing-off =
predictable end-of-dose decline; on-off = unpredictable switches) but the AAN
measurement set treats them as the same coded concept.
